body:
I wonder if this is intended. I poked around the code and the issue may be the [`equalArraysOrString`](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/616543ded07d632438185f3df6f3b73591cdaf80/packages/router/src/utils/collection.ts#L46) function that is called to determine if `queryParams` have changed, and if so to emit them.

The function doesn't do an index-by-index comparison. Rather it just makes sure that for each value in the first array, that value exists _anywhere_ in the 2nd array.

So `[4, 4, 2]` -> `[4, 3, 2]` does not emit because 4 and 2 exist in the 2nd array. The other way around works as expected `[4, 3, 2]` -> `[4, 4, 2]` because 3 does not exist in the 2nd array. 

So I suppose it may behave as you expect if [here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d1ea1f4c7f3358b730b0d94e65b00bc28cae279c/packages/router/src/router_state.ts#L417) it uses `deepEqual` instead of `shallowEqual`.

On further look, it seems `equalArraysOrString` was [created](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/828e5c1f79e53202be497fb57aa0b39bc3774300) for query params? In this case, does seem like a bug. I'll try a PR soon.

Yeah this strikes me as a bug. It needs to look for the same values with the same frequency but ignoring the order. [4, 4, 2] to [4, 3, 2] should be counted as a change for multiple reasons: the frequency of 4 is different and there's a new value 3.

## What is the current behavior?
The queryParams observable or queryParamMap observables were not being fired when the params were arrays that hit an edge case in the equality check.

The `equalArraysOrString` function doesn't do an index-by-index comparison. Rather it just makes sure that for each value in the first array, that value exists anywhere in the 2nd array.

So [4, 4, 2] -> [4, 3, 2] does not emit because 4 and 2 exist in the 2nd array. The other way around works as expected [4, 3, 2] -> [4, 4, 2] because 3 does not exist in the 2nd array.

Issue Number:  #37709


## What is the new behavior?
Now the equality check for arrays ensures that both arrays have the same frequency of values in any order.
